Notification envelope, Chain routing and MessageQueue core — independent Go candidate

Scope and evidence

This ignored module is not registered in formal App/catalog/SDK and has made no
real message, site, login, downloader or media call. Product code is Go only.
Python is used exclusively by the source-only reference generator. Five complete
MoviePilot source copies are byte-identical to the actual installed files; the
reference records their SHA256 values and the actual Python3.12.13,
Pydantic2.13.4/pydantic-core2.46.4 versions. Original Notification AST is executed
with the real installed Pydantic and original enums, not a constructor stub.
Original Chain and MessageQueue method statements run with recording DB/config/
user/event/sender dependencies; no app imports, real runtime configuration,
background thread, credential, network request or channel sender is involved.

reference/installed-oracle.json contains:
353 complete Notification constructions, 794 compact integer lexical cases,
19 schedule parse cases, 84 windows, 11 time-to-minutes cases,
6 synchronous sends, 6 actual async function bodies, 6 monitor iterations,
18 normal route cases, 16 failure-prefix/argument cases and 3 actual Chain+Queue
composition cases. The async oracle uses a recording executor returning a
completed awaitable: it proves branch/argument behavior, not asyncio scheduling.

The compact integer matrix exposed differences a regex+int approximation missed.
String coercion follows the two parsing attempts and cleanup order from the
version-tagged official Pydantic source and pinned jiter0.14.0 NumberInt parser.
The crate archive checksum matches that release Cargo.lock. Their MIT licenses
are retained. This is the consumed integer subset, not a port of all jiter or
Pydantic. See reference/dependencies.json for exact sources and checksums.
Official primary source:
https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/v2.13.4/pydantic-core/src/input/shared.rs

Exact Go API

NewEnvelope(Object) (*Envelope,error), Envelope.Dump() Object and Get(string) any.
Object values must be JSON-shaped. Constructor ignores extra fields and preserves
all installed defaults, nulls, union string/int distinctions, ordered validation
error types/locations, nested buttons and enum values. json.Number retains large
integers. Errors omit raw user values. It does not emulate arbitrary Python
objects, byte strings, Decimal/Fraction, Pydantic error wording/URLs, or model
mutation aliases. Zero Envelope is invalid; construct it explicitly. Dump/Get
return owned JSON values. The source's post-construction recipient assignment is
not revalidated; UserSettings nil differs from an empty map.

ParseSchedule(any) ([]Period,error), TimeToMinutes(string) (*big.Int,error),
Allowed([]Period,time.Time) bool. Period is [4]*big.Int; no implicit hour/minute
range validation is added. Python3.12 Unicode15 integer/strip/lower behavior is
read from the frozen formal legacyanime package where source needs Python rules;
Pydantic's string integer conversion uses its separate ASCII/Rust cleanup rules.
Truthy non-map schedule entries raise source AttributeError outside the parse
try. Invalid start/end values inside that try skip only that period. Endpoints
are inclusive, equal endpoints allow one minute, overnight wraps midnight.

NewQueue(periods,now,systemStopped,callback) (*Queue,error).
Queue.Send / AsyncSend(ctx,Call) (Attempt,error), Tick(ctx) []Attempt,
Pending() []Call, SetPeriods([]Period) error, Stop(). Call has Args and Kwargs.
Immediately is popped, and Python truth semantics apply (string "false" forces
send). Callback exceptions are exposed as an internal attempt observation but
are consumed without retry, as source _send catches them. Attempted is never a
remote delivery acknowledgment; absent callback is a no-op. Tick is one source
monitor iteration and checks the clock before and between FIFO entries. Calls
are removed before callback. Shared queue data is synchronized; no lock is held
while callback executes. Caller owns callback concurrency/cancellation.
This is an in-memory core, with no daemon, wait loop, persistent FIFO or recovery.
Stop disables subsequent Tick iterations; it cannot join a nonexistent source
thread. Explicit Send after Stop remains allowed. The trusted host owns its
existing worker/timer and must wait/cancel that worker before shutdown.

Router{Dependencies}.Post(ctx,*Envelope,Business,kwargs) error.
Dependencies: Now, Superuser, Render, SaveHistory, NotificationSwitch,
UserSettings, NoticeMessage, QueueCall. All dependencies belong to the trusted
host, never worker-supplied code/targets. Business carries the four original
host-side metadata objects; no metadata projection/template semantics are claimed.
Render is an unported complete MessageTemplateHelper dependency. Without it,
preformatted messages and messages with no ctype retain source bypass behavior;
a blank ctype-bearing message explicitly returns ErrTemplateDependency before
history/effects. Full Jinja/template selection/object projection/catch-and-assign
semantics and original caller mutation aliases are not implemented here.
A configured Render callback must implement that entire dependency itself;
a toy string substitution or success stub must not be registered as ready.

Original call order retained

1. current_time set only if absent, including preserving explicit null.
2. Render; nil message stops. An empty Notification object remains truthy.
3. SaveHistory once, before dispatch normalization/forks, unless save_history=false.
4. Deep copy dispatch; strip/lower internal string system userid to null.
5. If userid false and mtype true, read NotificationSwitch. Truthy non-string
   fails with source AttributeError after history. Split on comma without trim.
6. For each source action resolve targets, emit NoticeMessage, call QueueCall.
   Admin sends once; a repeated admin falls into the source break branch.
   Missing user means targets is exactly null, not {}. It falls back to admin
   once; after admin has already sent the missing user is skipped. Repeated
   user actions may emit multiple times; they are not silently deduplicated.
   Unknown/all/user-without-name stops isolation as source specifies.
7. If source chooses original dispatch, emit NoticeMessage before QueueCall;
   only this original call explicitly passes immediately=truth(userid).
   Isolated calls leave immediately absent, unless caller kwargs supplied it.

NoticeMessage data contains every field except save_history, plus type=mtype;
both type and mtype are present. Channel does not bypass Chain isolation.
Recipients/default admin/source/plugin IDs are not invented by this candidate.
Source plugin base link fallback belongs to a trusted producer adapter, not this
Chain method. Fixed plugin-page link and source mtype must be reconstructed from
authenticated producer identity as already documented in RemoveLink audit.

NoticeMessage is queued BEFORE MessageQueue window evaluation. Event consumers
such as MergeMessageNotify can run outside the core send window; do not delay the
whole event stream until NotificationSendTime. The actual EventManager enqueues
broadcasts and later dispatches subscribers via an executor. Its return is not a
subscriber receipt. This candidate invokes only that interface, not consumers.
LarkMessager is a MessageChain module, not a NoticeMessage subscriber. These are
separate routes and must have separate consumer/transport readiness and receipts.

Minimum safe App entry and required durability work

0. Construct/validate the full Envelope at the ORIGINAL source Notice call,
   before Chain/history and before returning to subsequent plugin effects.
   Original Base.post_message constructs Notification immediately. Invalid
   channel/mtype/field values fail that call and must prevent later source
   config/history operations; deferring first validation until a background
   handoff incorrectly changes the failure prefix. Persist the exact validated
   complete envelope sealed; do not reconstruct it from a cleaned public inbox
   title/message subset. Existing history_saved records need their original
   complete sealed producer envelope, not a public-record round trip.
1. Authenticate exact original committed outbox/core receipt and payload binding
   (producer instance/generation/effect identity/digest). Historical retired
   producers can hand over committed facts but get no new mutation authority.
   Rebuild Envelope from sealed exact source defaults; no universal worker
   notify RPC that can fabricate plugin origin, userid, recipients or link.
2. Reuse existing history_saved sealed handoff. A SaveHistory adapter must verify
   its exact envelope/record receipt and return the same receipt without adding
   another record or changing original time/read state. Source history is once
   before all forks, not once per channel or subscriber.
3. Persist the first kwargs current_time and the trusted routing snapshot/read
   receipts. Preserve absent/null/empty. Replaying route execution against new
   user/switch configuration can change fanout and resend a previous prefix.
4. Journal each dependency stage in order: history, switch read, user-settings
   read, NoticeMessage publication, core QueueCall acceptance. IDs bind original
   intent+route-index+stage+payload digest. An existing exact receipt replays the
   original response; conflicts fail. A published event references private sealed
   data and independent per-consumer receipts. Domain-event acceptance cannot
   acknowledge Merge/Lark or a remote channel. There is no catch-all delivered.
5. Core QueueCall must reserve capacity and persist full owned call in the same
   transaction as queue-accepted receipt. It only accepts fixed post_message,
   with trusted current schedule/timezone and no worker-selected recipient.
   Persisted FIFO requires monotonic insertion sequence; source time window is
   reevaluated at drain. Do not hold lifecycle/plugin/SQL locks during send.
6. For external attempts, persist intent before network, exact response/receipt
   after, and unknown after reply loss; never blindly replay unknown sends.
   Source catches errors and consumes rows, which is not a reliable negative ack.
   Each actual sender needs its own grant, fixed origin/TLS/credential boundary,
   budget and response/readback contract. Queue callback success alone is not a
   remote delivered fact. Full remote exactly-once is not promised by source.
7. Preflight whole encoded frame, envelope/targets, fanout and journal capacity
   before any new effect. Wire frames have explicit negotiated protocol limits;
   this pure module does not exempt them, truncate bodies, or weaken limits.
   Retain private bodies/target IDs sealed; log only opaque IDs/status/digests.

Router.Post and Queue are NOT durable idempotent drivers. Do not register a tick
that blindly reruns Post for every pending row. They are source behavior cores
for a journaled host adapter. No active owner/run proof, SQL receipt backend,
transport/recipient grant, persistent queue, MessageTemplate, MessageOper DB/SSE,
MessageHelper TTL/SSE, MergeMessageNotify transport or Lark transport is supplied.
Until those concrete dependencies exist, the only safe formal acceptance remains
history_saved with NoticeMessage/external stages explicitly pending. This module
can be migrated as additive pure algorithms without pretending those later
stages have been delivered.

Validation

verification.json pins commands, terminal outcomes, case counts and the source
manifest. Only this independent module is compiled; no App build/test, real user
service, real credential, external sender or original project write occurred.
Go normal/race/vet validate this scope only; no NAS or production readiness claim.
